- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 3–8% in next 2–3 periods.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias — adjust downward by 1–3% per period until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early mean reversion; if sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, reduce forecast slope sharply.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” oscillations (e.g., 1.00 → 0.33 → 1.00), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing midpoint.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses momentum; add 1–3% momentum bias to forecast if trend persists.
